questions.q: If I had studied harder, I ___ a better job now.
questions.explanation: Past condition with present result: past perfect + would + infinitive.

questions.q: If she were more careful, she ___ the accident last week.
questions.explanation: Present condition with past result: past simple + would have + past participle.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If he didn't miss the bus, he'd be here now.
If he hadn't missed the bus, he'd have been here now.
If he wouldn't have missed the bus, he'd be here now.
If he hadn't missed the bus, he'd be here now.
questions.explanation: A past condition affecting the present mixes past perfect with 'would be'.

questions.q: If I spoke better French, I ___ the job last month.
questions.explanation: Present ability with a past result needs 'would have + past participle'.

questions.q: If they hadn't moved to London, they ___ each other.
questions.explanation: A past condition with a past result uses 'would have + past participle'.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If you hadn't been so tired, you could have come with us.
If you weren't so tired, you could come with us.
If you wouldn't be so tired, you could have come with us.
If you weren't so tired, you could have come with us.
questions.explanation: A present state with a missed past chance mixes past simple and 'could have'.

questions.q: If I had more money, I ___ that car yesterday.
questions.explanation: A present wish about a past event: past simple + would have bought.

questions.q: She'd be a doctor now if she ___ medical school.
questions.explanation: The if-clause of a mixed conditional uses the past perfect for a past condition.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If it didn't rain, we would be playing tennis now.
If it hadn't rained, we would have played tennis now.
If it wouldn't have rained, we would be playing tennis now.
If it hadn't rained, we would be playing tennis now.
questions.explanation: Past condition, present result: past perfect in the if-clause, 'would be' in the main clause.

questions.q: If he were honest, he ___ about it last night.
questions.explanation: A general present condition with a past result needs 'would have told'.

questions.q: We'd be lost if you ___ the map.
questions.explanation: The if-clause takes the past perfect for the earlier condition.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If she had taken the job, she'd be living in Paris now.
If she took the job, she'd be living in Paris now.
If she had taken the job, she'd have lived in Paris now.
If she would have taken the job, she'd be living in Paris now.
questions.explanation: This mixes a past if-clause with a present continuous result.

questions.q: If I ___ taller, I could have reached the shelf.
questions.explanation: A present unreal condition uses the past simple, 'were' for all persons.

questions.q: They would have won if their captain ___ injured.
questions.explanation: The past condition in the if-clause needs the past perfect.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If you listened to me, you wouldn't be in trouble now.
If you had listened to me, you wouldn't be in trouble now.
If you had listened to me, you wouldn't have been in trouble now.
If you would have listened to me, you wouldn't be in trouble now.
questions.explanation: A past condition with a present result mixes past perfect and 'wouldn't be'.

questions.q: If she spoke Chinese, she ___ the contract last year.
questions.explanation: Present ability plus past result: past simple + would have signed.

questions.q: He'd be healthier now if he ___ smoking.
questions.explanation: The if-clause needs the past perfect for the earlier past condition.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If I hadn't overslept, I wouldn't be rushing now.
If I didn't oversleep, I wouldn't be rushing now.
If I hadn't overslept, I wouldn't have rushed now.
If I wouldn't have overslept, I wouldn't be rushing now.
questions.explanation: A past cause with a present effect mixes past perfect with 'wouldn't be'.

questions.q: If they ___ earlier, they would be here by now.
questions.explanation: The earlier past condition takes the past perfect in the if-clause.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If we booked sooner, we'd have better seats now.
If we had booked sooner, we'd have had better seats now.
If we had booked sooner, we'd have better seats now.
If we would have booked sooner, we'd have better seats now.
questions.explanation: This mixes a past perfect if-clause with a present result clause.
